subject: community-medicine
title: Fertility Measures: TFR, GFR, NRR and Replacement Level

steps.title: Crude birth rate and its crudeness
steps.tx: The **crude birth rate** (live births per 1000 mid-year population) fell in India from 40.8 in 1951 to 19.5 in 2020 on the programme's historical ledger. It is crude because the denominator includes men, children and the elderly who cannot give birth, so fertility comparisons between populations need refined measures that follow this lesson.
steps.say: Births per thousand everyone: forty point eight in 1951, nineteen point five in 2020 nationally. Crude, because most of the denominator cannot deliver. Refined measures exist precisely for fair comparison.

steps.title: General and age-specific fertility
steps.tx: **General fertility rate** counts live births per 1000 women aged 15 to 49, removing non-reproductive population from the denominator. Age-specific rates then expose the reproductive curve's shape: early peaks signal early marriage and childbearing patterns, delayed peaks signal postponement, and the curve's area is the next measure.
steps.say: Restrict the denominator to women fifteen to forty nine and comparison sharpens. Age-specific curves then expose timing: early peaks accuse early childbearing, delayed peaks show postponement.

nodes.label: Divided by women in each age group

steps.title: Total fertility rate: children per woman
steps.tx: The **total fertility rate** sums age-specific rates across 15 to 49 to give children per woman surviving the reproductive span at current rates: India fell from 6.0 in 1951 to 2.0 in NFHS 2019-21, below the classic replacement level of 2.1 nationally while several states remain above it. State, residence and education gradients hide inside the national average.
steps.say: Sum the curve: children per woman. Six in 1951, two point zero nationally in the latest family health survey, below replacement on average with states still above. Averages hide gradients examiners probe.

steps.tx: The **total fertility rate** adds age specific fertility rates from ages fifteen to forty nine. The sum is the number of children a woman would have if she lived through her reproductive years at current rates. India moved from 6.0 in 1951 to 2.0 in NFHS 2019 to 2021, below the classic replacement level of 2.1 for the country as a whole. Several states remain above replacement. State, rural or urban residence, and education hide inside that national average.
steps.say: Total fertility sums age specific rates from fifteen to forty nine into children per woman. India fell from 6.0 in 1951 to 2.0 in NFHS 2019 to 2021, under the 2.1 replacement mark nationally, while some states stay above it. Residence and schooling sit inside the average.

vis.alt: A curve shows the India total fertility rate falling from 6.0 in 1951 through 2.1 to 2.0.
vis.caption: A fertility curve falls from six children per woman in 1951 to about two in the latest national survey. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Replacement level and NRR
steps.tx: **Replacement fertility** (TFR about 2.1) lets each generation exactly replace itself, the extra tenth covering girls who die before reproducing and sex ratio at birth. Net reproduction rate refines it directly: daughters surviving to reproduce per newborn girl, with NRR of 1 the exact replacement signal demographers certify.
steps.say: Two point one replaces generations: the extra tenth covers mortality before motherhood. Net reproduction counts surviving daughters directly; exactly one means exact replacement certified.

steps.title: Why population keeps growing below replacement
steps.tx: **Population momentum** keeps births exceeding deaths for decades after fertility falls, because yesterday's large birth cohorts now occupy reproductive ages while deaths concentrate in small old cohorts. India stabilisation is projected around 2045 in national goals despite replacement fertility already reached. Momentum, not fertility failure, explains continued growth in stems.
steps.say: Growth outlives its cause. Large young cohorts reproduce while small old cohorts die, so births exceed deaths for decades after replacement. Stabilisation near 2045 is momentum arithmetic, not programme failure.

nodes.label: Past high fertility built large cohorts

steps.tx: **Population momentum** keeps births above deaths for decades after fertility has already fallen. Large birth cohorts from earlier years now sit in the reproductive ages, while deaths are concentrated in much smaller older cohorts. The national goal places Indian stabilisation around 2045 even though replacement fertility has already been reached for the country. Continued growth in a stem is therefore momentum arithmetic, not evidence that the fertility programme failed.
steps.say: After fertility falls, big cohorts born earlier are still of childbearing age, and the elderly cohorts dying are small. Births therefore exceed deaths for decades. Indian stabilisation near 2045 is that momentum, not a failure to reach replacement.

vis.alt: A diagram shows large young cohorts entering reproductive ages while births still outnumber deaths.
vis.caption: Wide young age bands enter childbearing years while births remain above deaths. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Couple protection and unmet need
steps.tx: **Couple protection rate** (eligible couples effectively protected by contraception) rose from 10.4 percent in 1971 to over half by recent surveys, while unmet need (fecund women wanting to space or limit but not using) persists near a tenth of married women nationally. Method mix skew (female sterilisation dominant, spacing methods thin) is the quality critique attached to the numbers.
steps.say: Protection climbed fivefold since 1971 while unmet need persists near a tenth. Sterilisation dominates the method mix and spacing stays thin: the quality critique stapled to every quantity gain.

rows: Wanting space or limit, not using
Sterilisation heavy, spacing thin in India

steps.title: Determinants: marriage age, literacy, mortality
steps.tx: **Fertility determinants** interlock: raising girls' marriage age beyond 18 (preferably 20 in national goals), female literacy, and infant survival (IMR toward 28 per 1000 in demographic goals) each depress desired and actual fertility. Son preference sustains progression to another pregnancy after daughters, the cultural determinant surveys still measure state by state.
steps.say: Levers interlock. Later marriage, literate mothers, surviving infants shrink desired families. Son preference drives one more pregnancy after daughters. Goals name eighteen minimum, twenty preferred, mortality in the twenties.

steps.title: Gross versus net reproduction
steps.tx: **Gross reproduction rate** counts daughters born per woman ignoring mortality; net reproduction subtracts girls lost before reproductive age. Where mortality is high the pair diverge widely; where survival is near-universal they converge, which is why NRR loses discriminating drama in low-mortality settings and TFR headlines instead.
steps.say: Daughters born versus daughters surviving: gross ignores deaths, net subtracts them. High mortality splits the pair; near-universal survival merges them. Headlines therefore follow the simpler total rate.

steps.title: Reading a fertility stem
steps.tx: Stems fingerprint measures by denominator words: **per 1000 population** names crude birth rate, per 1000 women 15 to 49 names general fertility, children per woman names TFR, daughters surviving names NRR, and couples protected names a programme output rather than fertility itself. Extracting the denominator phrase before calculating rescues most demography marks.
steps.say: Denominators fingerprint every measure. Thousand population, thousand reproductive women, children per woman, surviving daughters, couples protected. Read the denominator phrase first; arithmetic follows safely.
